description: Spatial technique owner: CRS/EPSG/SRID, reprojection, ITM/WGS84/UTM, geometry validity (ST_MakeValid, shapely), predicates, spatial joins, buffers, indexing (R-tree/GiST), PostGIS, GeoPandas, DuckDB Spatial, rasters, zonal stats, resampling, COG/STAC/GeoParquet/FlatGeobuf/Zarr, GeoAI pipelines (spatial CV, leakage, tiling/chipping, segmentation, detection). Rendering → web-map-builder; delivery format → apex-geoai-style.

results.query: i've got a geodataframe of ~40k parcel polygons loaded from parcels.gpkg in EPSG:4326 and i need to compute the area of each one in dunams, then flag any parcel whose geometry is invalid before i do a spatial join against the zoning layer. what's the right order of operations here and which CRS should i be in?

my building-footprint segmentation model gets 0.91 IoU on validation but falls apart on a new city. i split the chips randomly with train_test_split. is that the problem, and how should i be splitting instead?
spatial join in geopandas is taking 40+ minutes joining 2.1M GPS pings against ~5,000 statistical-area polygons. both are in ITM. what am i doing wrong

im using scipy cKDTree to find the nearest clinic for each of 300k household points, coords are lat/lon straight out of the csv. results look fine in the middle of the country but wrong up north. any idea why

need mean NDVI per municipality from a 10m sentinel composite covering all of israel. ~260 polygons, raster is about 18GB. currently looping over polygons with rasterio mask and it's going to take all night

we have 12M address points that get re-queried constantly by an analytics dashboard. currently a 4GB shapefile on a network share (yes i know). what format should we move to and why — considering duckdb and pandas both need to read it
quick sanity check: i did gdf.buffer(500) on a WGS84 layer expecting a 500m buffer and the output polygons are enormous, they cover half the country. what happened

resampling a 30m land cover classification down to 100m for a regional summary. gdal.Warp with bilinear gave me class values like 3.7 which obviously aren't real classes. what resampling should i actually use here
converting survey points between ITM (2039) and WGS84 with pyproj and everything lands consistently ~150m off. the offset is systematic, not random. transformer is built once and reused
im chipping 0.5m orthophotos into 512x512 tiles to train a solar-panel detector. should the tiles overlap, and how do i stop the same rooftop appearing in both train and val?
the legend on my leaflet choropleth keeps covering the data in the south of the map on mobile. whats a good way to position it so it doesn't occlude anything at 375px width
im mapping median household income by statistical area and cant decide between quantile and natural breaks for the classification. which gives a more honest looking map
about to make the repo public — need og:image and og:description set up so the link preview renders properly when i share it in a whatsapp group
can you set up branch protection on main for this repo, require one approving review and passing status checks before merge
starting a new dashboard frontend. should i reach for zustand or just use react context here? there's maybe 6 pieces of shared state and one of them updates on every mouse move
review the endpoint layout in api/routers/parcels.py — im not sure the response models are structured right and there's no pagination on the list endpoint yet
i have two csvs, customers.csv and orders.csv, both have a customer_id column. need to join them and get total order value per customer, output as a new csv
this postgres query takes 8 seconds: SELECT * FROM events WHERE tenant_id = $1 AND created_at > $2 ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 50. there's an index on tenant_id. how do i speed it up
want to segment our ~50k customers into groups based on purchase frequency, average basket size and recency. thinking kmeans but not sure how to pick k
my gradient boosting model is clearly overfitting — train R2 0.94, test 0.61. should i be using k-fold cross validation instead of a single holdout split, and does that even help with overfitting?
